layers.title: Aspect (downslope direction)
layers.measures: Direction the ground faces, i.e. the compass bearing of steepest DESCENT, degrees clockwise from north (0 = faces north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west), Horn 3x3 finite difference on the 2 m elevation (about 6 m support), same gradient as slope_2m. 'North-facing' means aspect_deg within 45 deg of 0 (or aspect_class N / NE / NW).

layers.title: Plan curvature (smoothed)
layers.measures: Curvature of the contour line across the slope (spurs / ridges diverge = positive, gullies / hollows converge = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. (Zevenbergen and Thorne's raw plan-curvature formula has the opposite sign to their profile formula; plan is flipped here so both read the same way.)

layers.title: Profile curvature (smoothed)
layers.measures: Curvature of the surface along the downslope direction (convex breaks of slope at the top of scarps = positive, concave bases = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. (Zevenbergen and Thorne's raw plan-curvature formula has the opposite sign to their profile formula; plan is flipped here so both read the same way.)

layers.title: Distance to Perseverance traverse
layers.measures: Euclidean distance from the cell centre to the nearest point of the Perseverance traverse line (traverse.geojson, NASA MMGIS drive segments, straight lines between published vertices).

layers.title: Distance to geologic-unit contact
layers.measures: Euclidean distance from the cell centre to the nearest boundary between two different mapped geologic units (cells touching a different known unit; the boundary with 'no polygon' is not a contact).

layers.title: Elevation (MOLA-referenced)
layers.measures: Surface elevation above the MOLA areoid (delta-geoid corrected), 1 m HiRISE stereo DTM averaged to 2 m; CTX 20 m DTM (bilinear) where HiRISE has no data.

layers.title: Local relief (200 m radius)
layers.measures: Maximum minus minimum elevation within 200 m of each cell: highlights large landforms (delta-front scarps, crater rim, mesa edges) against flat floor.

layers.title: Local relief (50 m radius)
layers.measures: Maximum minus minimum elevation within 50 m (disc, centre to cell-centre distance) of each cell: a proxy for the height of a scarp, cliff or incised wall in the neighbourhood.

layers.title: CRISM mineral diversity (100 m)
layers.measures: Number of distinct CRISM mineral layers (of 7: carbonate, olivine, Fe/Mg-smectite, high-Ca pyroxene, low-Ca pyroxene, kaolinite, Mg-smectite-2) with at least one cell of tier >= weak_orbital within 100 m (integer stored as float). Counts layers, not independent minerals: mixed prototypes appear in more than one layer, and pyroxene/smectite variants count separately.

layers.title: Outcrop exposure (steep-face relief)
layers.measures: Height proxy for an exposed vertical section: local_relief_50m where at least 2% of the cells within 50 m have slope_2m >= 25 degrees (a steep face is actually present in the window), else 0. High values mean tall steep walls nearby, the places where stratigraphy can be seen in section.

layers.title: Roughness (5x5 elevation std)
layers.measures: Standard deviation of elevation in a 5x5 cell (10 m) window, no plane removal, so on tilted ground it includes the slope contribution.

layers.title: Slope over 2 m grid (Horn)
layers.measures: Surface slope from the 2 m elevation, Horn 3x3 finite difference (about 6 m support).

layers.title: Topographic position index (50 m disc)
layers.measures: Cell elevation minus the mean elevation of the other cells within 50 m (disc, centre excluded) on the 2 m grid. Positive = above its surroundings (ridge, crest, mesa top), negative = below (hollow, channel, crater floor next to a rim), about 0 = flat or mid-slope.

layers.title: Terrain ruggedness index (3x3)
layers.measures: Riley et al. ruggedness: square root of the summed squared elevation differences between a cell and its 8 neighbours (2 m cells, 6 m window). Unit is metres; includes the slope contribution (a smooth 30 deg ramp has a high TRI).

layers.title: Geologic unit diversity (100 m)
layers.measures: Number of distinct mapped geologic units having at least one cell within 100 m of the cell (integer stored as float). 1 = deep inside one unit, 2+ = near a contact, 3+ = junctions.

layers.title: Aspect class (8-way + flat)
layers.measures: Eight 45-degree compass sectors of aspect_deg (N = 337.5-22.5, NE = 22.5-67.5, ...) plus 'flat' where slope < 1 degree. Query 'north-facing slopes' as aspect_class in [N, NE, NW] (or == N for strictly north).

layers.measures: Mapped geologic unit at each cell from the USGS geologic map of Jezero crater and the Nili Planum region (1:75,000, polygon layer GeoUnits_v1), rasterised to the 2 m grid by polygon containment at the cell centre. Class names are the map's unit names with the map symbol in brackets.

pois.name: Sample 14: Shuyak
pois.description: Sample 14 of the NASA Perseverance sample list: core/sample 'Shuyak' from feature 'Amalik', sealed sol 575 (Oct. 2, 2022). Rock type per NASA list: Sedimentary (Rock Core). Sampling region per NASA list: Delta Front. APPROXIMATE position derived from the rover waypoint at sol 565 (RMC 29_0, MMGIS waypoint, the last waypoint at or before sol 575); NOT an official sample coordinate. The rover may have moved between that waypoint and coring; the chord to the next waypoint (sol 592) is 18 m, so treat the position as uncertain by at least 18 m. In-situ mineral statement (olivine; tier confirmed_in_situ marked within 18 m): Williams et al. 2023, LPSC 54 abstract (NTRS 20230000588): at Cape Nukshak 'primary mineral phases (olivine, pyroxenes) were detected by SCAM LIBS and VISIR'; Amalik is the location of cores Shuyak and Mageik. Hurowitz et al. 2023 (Goldschmidt, doi:10.7185/gold2023.18487): PIXL finds an 'altered olivine-dominated' source at the base of the Cape Nukshak section (Amalik member). Section-level statements applied at the sample site; no per-sample mineralogy was read. Williams et al. 2023 also report VISIR signatures at Amalik most consistent with a Mg-rich serpentine; serpentine is not an evidence layer here.
